lesson.child_mission: A fair friction ramp test keeps ramp height, object and release method the same, changing only the surface material.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same science idea to a new object or material, then compare two pieces of evidence for strength.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Which change would make the test unfair: taller ramp for sandpaper only? How fix?

FEEDBACK
Unfair — use the same height for every surface.

WATCH FOR
Pushing harder on the surface you expect to win ruins fairness.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Run the fair ramp test with three surfaces. Record distances. Conclude which had most friction with evidence. List what you kept the same.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.
lesson.learning_intention: A fair friction ramp test keeps ramp height, object and release method the same, changing only the surface material.
materials: Optional: safe everyday objects for observation
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.

Parent: Likely misconception: Pushing harder on the surface you expect to win ruins fairness. Keep sample answers out of the child role.
